dossier.agronomicSubtitle: Climate, canopy, cultural work, and productivity of the selected groves
dossier.agronomicLead: A technical reading of the year for the person who advises the groves. Figures are taken from the field register, the weather archive, recorded work, and posted harvests.
dossier.accountSubtitle: Gross output, classified costs, and the result of the holding
dossier.accountLead: A management account of what was received and what was paid during the year. It is arranged as a farm account: output, costs, net result, and the contribution of each grove.
dossier.traceSubtitle: Origin, lots, mill, quantities, and the grade recorded with each lot
dossier.traceLead: An operational record of fruit leaving the grove and oil returning from the mill. Each line is a posted harvest.
dossier.climateLead: Where a weather archive exists, area-weighted rainfall is {{rain}} and the area-weighted climatic balance is {{balance}}.

dossier.agronomicMethod: Method. Rain, temperature, frost (minimum at or below 0 °C), heat (maximum at or above 35 °C) and dry spells (days with at most 0.5 mm of rain) come from the grove weather archive. Water balance is rainfall minus reference evapotranspiration (ET₀), the climatic balance used in FAO-56. It is not soil moisture and it does not include irrigation. A deficit wider than 50 mm is marked Watch; wider than 150 mm is marked Outside range. A surplus is not marked as stress. NDVI is the canopy index stored for the year when a satellite review exists: below 0.25 Outside range, from 0.25 to 0.35 Watch, at or above 0.35 Within range. Oil yield is oil weight divided by olive weight where both were recorded: below 12% Outside range, from 12% to 16% Watch, at or above 16% Within range. These bands are indicative for an olive grove. They are not a diagnosis, a laboratory result, or a commercial grade.
dossier.accountMethod: Method. This is a management account of posted receipts and costs for the calendar year, in euro. It follows the shape of a farm account — gross output, classified costs, net result, result per hectare — and it is not a statutory financial statement, a tax return, or an accrual account. Costs are grouped as labour (including the harvest crew and the agronomist), growing inputs, mill and after harvest, and overhead. Unit costs divide total posted costs by the olive or oil kilograms on the harvest records. A receipt that was not given a category is shown as recorded receipts and is not treated as an oil sale.
dossier.traceMethod: Method. Each row is a posted harvest record: origin grove, date, method, olive weight, mill, and — where the mill confirmed them — oil kilograms and litres. Litres are never calculated from kilograms. Extraction is oil kilograms divided by the olive kilograms of the lots that have an oil weight. Lots without an oil weight remain in the olive total and are excluded from the extraction rate. The quality column is the grade entered with the record. This is an operational traceability record for the holding. It is not an official laboratory certificate, an invoice, or a declaration of conformity under olive-oil marketing rules.

brief.compareSubtitle: Yield, oil, cost, and result of the selected groves, set beside one another
brief.compareLead: A ranking inside this selection. The order is result per hectare. It is not a benchmark against other holdings or a regional average.
brief.compareMethod: Method. Groves are ordered by result per hectare, which is posted profit divided by recorded area. Oil yield uses the same indicative bands as the agronomic dossier: below 12% Outside range, from 12% to 16% Watch, at or above 16% Within range. Frost, heat, and the longest dry spell appear only where a yearly weather archive exists for that grove. There is no combined stress score. A grove that leads on cost per hectare is the most expensive in this selection, not the best managed.
brief.workSubtitle: What was finished, what is still open, and the cost posted to each grove
brief.workLead: A register of cultural work for the year. Counts come from the grove task record. The cost is the amount posted to the grove ledger. It is not a price attached to each task.
brief.workMethod: Method. Completed, open, and overdue counts are the task totals kept on each grove. Completion is completed work divided by completed plus open. The monthly bars sum completed tasks by month from the yearly work archive. The kind table shows how many tasks of each kind were finished against how many were planned. Costs recorded against a task kind are not shown: the only money in this register is the cost posted to the grove ledger.
